summary: In this fiction excerpt from Book 6, an unnamed narrator drives Arthur's sedan westward through a city chase while an SUV with a grenade-launcher gunner pursues them. The narrator jumps the car off a high bank into the concrete-lined Los Angeles River channel, then drives north along the riverbed. The pursuing SUV plunges into the cement, and the narrator, seeing the grenade's blast coming, swerves the car into the channel wall, where it flips onto its left side. The excerpt ends mid-sentence as the grenade hits.
one_line: A chase excerpt in which a narrator escapes an armed SUV by driving a sedan off a bank into the concrete Los Angeles River channel.
key_facts: The narrator drives a sedan that belongs to Arthur, and Arthur is in the car behind the narrator.
An SUV pursues the car, and its gunner tries to line up a shot with a grenade launcher.
The car hits a bank of railroad tracks and thumps over them, almost shaking loose from its frame.
The narrator describes the Los Angeles River in summer as a trickle of water through a wide, high-walled concrete ditch.
The narrator floors the gas pedal and the car sails off the high bank of the concrete trench.
The car lands belly-first on all four wheels on the bare cement at the bottom of the channel.
The narrator drives the sedan northward along the river and the car takes off like a shot.
The SUV flies out onto the edge, cannot stop in time, and its driver tries to brake.
The SUV flips into a nosedive and plunges headfirst into the cement.
The grenade launcher gunner aims and fires even while about to die in the crash.
The narrator sees the grenade's explosion, shock waves and concussion as concentric circles of force, and concludes that no possible move will be enough.
The narrator jerks the wheel and bounces the car into the wall of the concrete channel.
The car flips onto its left side and skids down the riverbed, with metal screaming and glass shattering.
The grenade hits, and the excerpt breaks off mid-sentence with the narrator saying 'I'd mooned it with'.
